RoomType.maps_to: driver.py's Event fight path (`_run_event`) always calls `_run_combat(event.pending_encounter, RoomType.MONSTER)` -- RoomType is hardcoded to MONSTER for every event-triggered fight, matching BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.cs:26's `RoomType.Monster`.

ShouldGiveRewards.maps_to: `Encounter.should_give_rewards` (monsters/base.py), explicitly set `should_give_rewards=False` on all three BATTLEWORN_DUMMY_SETTING_1/2/3 constants (battle_friend.py:73,77,81), matching BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.cs:28's override. Honoured end to end: driver.py's `_run_combat` gates the ENTIRE reward call (gold included, not just the screen) on `encounter.should_give_rewards`, and `conformance/runner.py` has the identical gate -- both mirror RewardsCmd.OfferForRoomEnd's `EmptyForRoom(room)` branch (RewardsCmd.cs:26-30) rather than only suppressing the UI. The event's own `resume_after_combat` (battleworn_dummy.py:62-94) grants the setting's real reward (potion/upgrades/relic) through a completely separate path, matching BattlewornDummy.cs's Resume, not this flag.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no sim field or property named this anywhere (checked: `grep -rn AllPossibleMonsters\|all_possible_monsters sts2_rl/` finds zero matches in the whole tree, for any encounter, not just this one -- nothing downstream currently asks 'what monsters could this encounter produce').
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: The wiring task modelled BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.cs's ONE class + Setting enum as three separate sim Encounter constants (harness.py's `_encounter_units` docstring gives the reasoning: no per-setting behaviour differs on any OTHER shared hook, so three records would drift with nothing to disagree about). AllPossibleMonsters (BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.cs:56-61, the union {BattleFriendV1,V2,V3}) has no single-object equivalent under that split, but each split constant's own `monster_classes` already answers 'what will THIS setting's visit produce' exactly -- there is no random branch inside a single Setting's GenerateMonsters, so nothing is lost per-instance. The only thing genuinely absent is a query across all three at once, and nothing in the sim ever asks that (see the empty grep above).

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: `battle_friend.py`'s three module-level `Encounter(...)` constants + the base `Encounter.create_monsters` (monsters/base.py) they use unmodified. Roster: exactly the one class the chosen setting names (BattleFriendV1/V2/V3), matching the switch at BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.cs:65-70 arm for arm. Order: trivially one element, matches. Slot: C# returns `(monster, null)` (line 71); the sim's constants declare no `slots`/`monster_slots`, so `create_monsters` never assigns `slot_name`, which stays at its Creature default (None) -- matches null. Draw count: BOTH sides draw ZERO from any Rng inside this method (the C# switch and the Python constant lookup are pure selection, no `base.Rng` call anywhere in the C# body) -- confirmed by reading BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.cs:63-72 top to bottom.

SaveCustomState.maps_to: no sim counterpart. `SaveCustomState`/`LoadCustomState` exist to persist `Setting`+`RanOutOfTime` across a save-and-reload into a PRE-FINISHED combat room (`CombatRoom.StartPreFinishedCombat`, called from the save/load path, not from a live run) -- a save-game feature. The sim (`snapshots.py`, checked in full) has no concept of a pre-finished combat room or of reloading mid-encounter at all; the headless RL/conformance architecture always plays a combat straight through in one process. `powers.py:3712-3714`'s `BattlewornDummyTimeLimitPower.on_enemy_side_end` has one dead branch that reads `hasattr(encounter, "ran_out_of_time")` -- always False, since the base `Encounter` dataclass has no such field -- but this is inert, not a divergence: the event's own `resume_after_combat` (battleworn_dummy.py:69) detects the flee outcome directly off `combat.enemies[0].escaped` (set unconditionally by `CreatureCmd.escape`, cmds.py:785), never off this dead attribute, so the SAME run-time outcome (no reward on a timed-out dummy) is reached by a different, always-live path.
SaveCustomState.rationale: Unreachable in the sim's headless, no-save-load architecture: there is no session-persistence layer for mid-run combat rooms anywhere in sts2_rl (checked snapshots.py in full, and grepped the whole tree for any reader of a comparable 'pre-finished combat' concept -- none exists), so the game feature this method exists to support has no operating mode in the sim at all, not even a partial one. The RUNTIME behaviour it exists to preserve (no reward for RanOutOfTime) is independently reproduced through `Creature.escaped`, so nothing is lost within a single continuous run -- only the save/quit/reload boundary itself is unmodelled.

LoadCustomState.maps_to: see SaveCustomState -- the load half of the same absent save-game feature.
LoadCustomState.rationale: Same as SaveCustomState: no save/reload-into-a-pre-finished-combat-room feature exists anywhere in the sim to receive this state.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39, inherited unchanged -- not re-overridden by BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.cs). The sim's `Encounter` dataclass is never registered as a combat hook listener anywhere: every `hooks.register(...)` call site in the tree targets a Player, Card, Affliction, Enchantment, Potion, Power, Relic, CombatHistory or Monster -- never an Encounter (checked every `hooks.register(` call site in the repo).

guards.what: encounter/_entry_slug_mismatch: `Encounter.entry` (monsters/base.py) is documented as `self.id.upper()`, which its own docstring says recovers the game's `ModelId.Entry` (`StringHelper.Slugify(type.Name)`, confirmed via `ModelDb.GetEntry`/`ModelId.cs`) 'for every encounter whose id matches its class-name slug'. All three BATTLEWORN_DUMMY_SETTING_1/2/3 ids do not: the one shared C# class slugifies to `BATTLEWORN_DUMMY_EVENT_ENCOUNTER`, but the three sim ids are `BATTLEWORN_DUMMY_SETTING_1/2/3`. This feeds `rng.make_encounter_rng(seed, floor, entry)` the wrong key in parity mode, so the per-encounter Rng this unit builds (`EncounterModel.Rng`, EncounterModel.cs:42-49's documented run-independent stream) is seeded to a different value than the game's. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py entry-slug-mismatch` -- prints MISMATCH for all three settings.
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `Encounter` gained an explicit `entry_slug` field and `Encounter.entry` returns it when set, so this unit seeds `make_encounter_rng` with the game's real `ModelId.Entry` while keeping its sim id. A mechanical sweep of ALL 87 sim encounters against `src/Core/Models/Encounters/*.cs` (audit/tools/encounter_entry_sweep.py) found two more the unit batches had not checked — `fuzzy_wurm_crawler` (FuzzyWurmCrawlerWeak) and `overgrowth_crawlers_normal` (OvergrowthCrawlers) — and now reports MATCH for every one. Pinned by test/test_encounter_entry_slugs.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: The per-encounter Rng this unit constructs is mis-seeded relative to the game in parity mode, but BattlewornDummyEventEncounter.GenerateMonsters draws ZERO values from `base.Rng` (confirmed above, and by `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py dormant-4-zero-draws`, which rebuilds each setting's monsters under two unrelated seeds and gets byte-identical results both times), so today the wrong seed has no observable consequence for this unit. Contrast `punch_off_event/G1` (the same mechanism, LIVE there) -- see that record.
